record_type: VENDOR ASSESSMENT — research, not a live account probe
question: Does Linode (Akamai Cloud) satisfy this build's compute requirements, given that Azure's risk is card verification?

REQUIREMENTS_THIS_WAS_SCORED_AGAINST.R1_platform: Linux x86_64, >=2 vCPU, >=8 GiB RAM, root SSH. megacmd is a native .deb binary and is the ONLY thing that can decrypt this corpus.
REQUIREMENTS_THIS_WAS_SCORED_AGAINST.R2_disk: >=350 GB. megacmd IGNORES the '::' subpath and fetches the ENTIRE 319.95 GB share, so the VM must stage all of it. This is the binding constraint and it is why GitHub Actions was ruled out.
REQUIREMENTS_THIS_WAS_SCORED_AGAINST.R3_region: EU, to keep MEGA -> VM -> api.eu.deepgram.com intra-EU.
REQUIREMENTS_THIS_WAS_SCORED_AGAINST.R4_payment: MUST survive a Nigerian card. Oracle already failed this; Azure may too. Verve Classic is reportedly domestic-only.
REQUIREMENTS_THIS_WAS_SCORED_AGAINST.R5_cost: Bounded, against the recorded compute waiver.
REQUIREMENTS_THIS_WAS_SCORED_AGAINST.R6_run_length: Hourly billing with a monthly cap, so a throwaway VM can be destroyed at completion.

R1_PLATFORM.evidence: Shared CPU plans run to 32 vCPU / 192 GB RAM / 3840 GB storage. Akamai Cloud supports Linux images with root SSH via the lish gateway.
R1_PLATFORM.why_it_matters: megacmd is the only decryption route. It is a native Debian/Ubuntu binary and installs unattended on any of these images.

R2_DISK — the binding constraint.verdict: PASS, but only on the 32 GB plan

plans.why_not: 320 GB against a 319.95 GB share is 99.98% full. Zero headroom for the OS, logs, or megacmd temp files. Would fail in practice, not on paper.

block_storage_alternative.arithmetic: Linode 8 GB ($0.072/hr x 72h = $5.18) + 400 GB block storage ($40.00)
block_storage_alternative.verdict: WORSE than simply running the 32 GB plan for 72h ($20.74). Block storage also bills monthly, so a 72-hour run pays a full month. Rejected.

R3_REGION.verdict: PASS — strongest EU coverage of any candidate
R3_REGION.note: Frankfurt is explicitly the busiest EU core region and has received dedicated capacity expansion. DigitalOcean offers only 3 EU regions by comparison.

R4_PAYMENT — THE DECIDING AXIS.verdict: PASS, and materially better than Azure
R4_PAYMENT — THE DECIDING AXIS.accepted_methods: All major credit cards, PLUS Google Pay and PayPal.
R4_PAYMENT — THE DECIDING AXIS.why_this_is_the_important_finding: It is a DIFFERENT FAILURE MODE, not a smaller version of the same one. If a Nigerian Verve card is rejected by card-network rules on Azure, PayPal or Google Pay funded from a different instrument is an independent path that Azure does not offer.
R4_PAYMENT — THE DECIDING AXIS.corroborating_evidence_of_the_risk_being: A 2026 Nigerian payment guide states plainly that 'Linode Nigerian Naira cards are usually declined for international payments, the fastest fix is a virtual dollar card funded with NGN/USDT.' So the card risk is REAL here too — but PayPal and Google Pay are the documented workaround, and that workaround exists.
R4_PAYMENT — THE DECIDING AXIS.billing_threshold: For new accounts the billing threshold begins at $50 and is adjusted automatically. Usage accrues against that threshold before a charge is raised.

R5_COST.currency_note: USD only. Any other currency requires a payment method that converts.
R5_COST.digitalocean_promotion: EUR 1.29 / 72h with 2000 GiB included (already researched; promotional, and promos vanish)
R5_COST.verdict: Linode is CHEAPER than Azure and roughly 16x the cost of the DigitalOcean promotion.
R5_COST.egress: Bundled transfer on the 32 GB plan is 16 TB. The run pushes ~182 GB to Deepgram and pulls ~184 GB from MEGA. Both are far inside the bundle, so egress cost is $0. Overage would be $0.005/GB, the cheapest in class.

R6_RUN_LENGTH.evidence: Hourly billing, rounded up to the nearest hour, with a monthly cap. Deleting the Linode stops the meter. Fits the throwaway-VM model exactly.

NO_HARD_SPEND_CAP.evidence: Independent 2026 review: 'nothing stops you spending past the credit. No hard cap pauses your servers at zero balance, so usage above the credit becomes an ordinary invoice.'
NO_HARD_SPEND_CAP.why_it_matters: This is the one genuine risk of choosing Linode. Under Rule 2, an unbounded meter is the wrong shape. A forgotten VM burning for a month costs ~$200, not ~$21.
NO_HARD_SPEND_CAP.MITIGATION: Destroy the Linode the moment the run completes, and check the Cloud Manager billing panel before leaving it unattended. The $50 new-account threshold also means nothing is charged until $50 accrues, so a short overrun is absorbed.
NO_HARD_SPEND_CAP.contrast: Azure's $200 trial credit is bounded. Linode's credit is not.

promotional_credit_unverified.evidence: A $100 promotional credit is advertised on akamai.com/lp/free-credit-100 and linode.com/lp/refer. An independent review warns Akamai 'has adjusted both the credit amount and the expiry window more than once' and that the offer 'can differ by region'.
promotional_credit_unverified.status: NOT VERIFIED LIVE. The figure on the signup page is the only one that binds. Do not plan against $100 until it is read off the page.
promotional_credit_unverified.policy_constraint: Akamai's promotional policy allows one promotional redemption per person/account.

MATERIAL DISADVANTAGES.block_storage_monthly_billing: Any block-storage-based disk strategy pays a full month regardless of run length.

VERDICT.does_it_fit: YES. It passes all six requirements.
VERDICT.is_it_better_than_azure: On the AXIS THAT MATTERS MOST — card verification — YES, because it accepts PayPal and Google Pay, which Azure does not. It is also cheaper (~$21 vs ~$26) and has more disk headroom (640 GB vs the 500 GB Azure would need).
VERDICT.is_it_safer_than_azure: NO. Azure's spend is bounded by a $200 credit; Linode's is not. A forgotten Linode is an unbounded bill.
VERDICT.RECOMMENDATION: Adopt Linode Frankfurt as the PRIMARY, not the fallback. The card-verification failure mode that most likely kills Azure is survivable on Linode, and the unbounded meter is controllable by destroying the instance on completion — which the run plan already requires. If the operator prefers a bounded meter over a wider payment surface, keep Azure first and hold Linode as the card-failure fallback.
VERDICT.what_would_settle_it: One live visit to the signup page to read the actual credit amount and expiry, and to see which payment methods are offered for a Nigeria-billed account.

NOT_VERIFIED: The live promotional credit amount and expiry — read off the signup page, not from a review.
Whether PayPal or Google Pay can actually be attached to a Nigeria-billed Linode account. Documented as accepted generally; not confirmed for this billing location.
Actual run duration, which determines whether the run costs $21 or $48.
MEGA -> Frankfurt -> api.eu.deepgram.com throughput, which governs run length and therefore total cost.
